1009	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1010	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1011	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1012	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1013	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1014	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1015	#
1016	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1017	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1018	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1019	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1020	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1021	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1022	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1023	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1024	_render_stage_divider() {
1025	    local stage="$1"
1026	    local width
1027	    width="$(_term_width)"
1028	    local color
1029	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1030	    local label=" ${stage} "
1031	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1032	
1033	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1034	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1035	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1036	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1037	
1038	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1039	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1040	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1041	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1042	        local bar
1043	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1044	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1045	        {
1046	            printf '\n'
1047	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1048	            printf '\n'
1049	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1050	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1051	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1052	            printf '\n'
1053	        } >&2
1054	        return 0
1055	    fi
1056	
1057	    local lbar rbar
1058	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1059	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1060	    {
1061	        printf '\n'
1062	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1063	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1064	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1065	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1066	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1067	        printf '\n'
1068	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1069	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1070	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1071	        printf '\n'
1072	    } >&2
1073	}
1074	
1075	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1076	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1077	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1078	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1079	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1080	#
1081	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1082	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1083	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1084	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1085	#
1086	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1087	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1088	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1089	#     banner=best-effort).
1090	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1091	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1092	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1093	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1094	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1095	#
1096	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1097	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1098	
1099	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1100	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1101	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1102	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1103	_render_cycle_entry() {
1104	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1105	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1106	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1107	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1108	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1109	    local bar
1110	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1111	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1112	    {
1113	        printf '\n'
1114	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1115	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1116	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1117	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1118	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1119	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1120	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1121	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1122	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1123	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1124	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1125	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1126	        fi
1127	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1128	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1129	        printf '\n'
1130	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1131	}
1132	
1133	# ─── _render_parallel_entry <group_id> <max_parallel> <members_csv> ──────────
1134	# ADR-039 (#1131): clone of _render_cycle_entry for a parallel stage group.
1135	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering parallel group <id>` line + DIM
1136	# trailer (max_parallel + members). Emitted by the runner BEFORE
1137	# parallel_group_run so the operator's eye finds the group boundary first.
1138	_render_parallel_entry() {
1139	    local group_id="$1" max="$2" members_csv="${3:-}"
1140	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1141	    local label=" parallel: ${group_id} "
1142	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1143	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1144	    local bar
1145	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1146	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1147	    {
1148	        printf '\n'
1149	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1150	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1151	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1152	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1153	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1154	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1155	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1156	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1157	        printf '\n'
1158	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1159	}
1160	
1161	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1162	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1163	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1164	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1165	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1166	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1167	    {
1168	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1169	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1170	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1171	}
1172	
1173	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1174	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1175	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1176	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1177	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1178	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1179	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1180	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1181	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1182	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1183	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1184	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1185	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1186	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1187	    local label
1188	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1189	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1190	    else
1191	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1192	    fi
1193	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1194	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1195	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1196	    local bar
1197	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1198	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1199	    {
1200	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1201	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1202	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1203	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1204	}
1205	
1206	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1207	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1208	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1209	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1210	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1211	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1212	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1213	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1214	    {
1215	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1216	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1217	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1218	}
1219	
1220	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1221	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1222	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1223	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1224	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1225	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD
1226	#   divergence      → ✗ RED+BOLD

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#
93	# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
127	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
129	    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
130	    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
131	    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start
140	    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
141	    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
142	    return 0
143	}
144	
145	# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
146	zbuild_pg_kill() {
147	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
148	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
149	    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
150	    local _self
151	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
152	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
153	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
154	}
155	
156	# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
157	# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
158	# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
159	zbuild_pid_kill() {
160	    local _pid="${1:-}"
161	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
162	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
163	}

content.content:
1	id: simple
2	name: Simple Pipeline
3	extends: null
4	
5	# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
6	merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged
7	
8	defaults:
9	  strategy: map
10	
11	# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12	# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
13	# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator,
14	# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
15	# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
16	#
17	# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
18	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
19	# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
20	# mechanical gates + gate-aggregator; the objective-gate plugin was then removed
21	# in B7 (#1139). The single merge-blocking construct is the gate-aggregator
22	# verdict (ADR-040 §5), reached via the cycle's exit_when.
23	#
24	# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
25	# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
26	# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
27	# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
28	# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
29	# one work unit per lens element — followed by
30	# `review-aggregator`, which merges the per-lens results into ONE advisory
31	# merge-readiness report. The lens group is ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
32	# exit_when/convergence (that remains the gate-aggregator, ADR-040 §5) and never
33	# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
34	flow:
35	  - hydrate
36	  - intake
37	  - plan
38	  - delivery_loop
39	  - review_lenses
40	  - review-aggregator
41	  - pr
42	
43	# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
45	# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
46	#
47	# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
48	# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
49	# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
50	# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
51	# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
52	# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
53	# called.
54	#
55	# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
56	# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
57	# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
58	#
59	# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
60	# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
61	# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
62	# quietly running nothing.
63	always_run:
64	  - release
65	  - persist
66	
67	# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
68	# One outer loop holds the design loop and the build loop. Every stage sees
69	# every finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine
70	# never decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
71	#   - A design loop that runs out of rounds ends this round (build is skipped)
72	#     and this loop goes round. When this loop's rounds are spent, the run stops.
73	delivery_loop:
74	  type: cycle
75	  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
76	  flow:
77	    - design_verify_cycle
78	    - build_test_cycle
79	  exit_when:
80	    all:
81	      - { stage: design_verify_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
82	      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
83	  max_iterations: 2
84	  on_max: halt
85	
86	# ─── design_verify_cycle (cycle) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
87	# ADR-046 (#1218, EPIC #1216): give the design stage an independent verifier that
88	# loops back TO it BEFORE the build cycle — so design/contract defects are caught
89	# where they are authored, not deep in the build cycle. Modelled on standard.yaml's
90	# design_impact_cycle (standard.yaml:40-67), which simple.yaml historically lacked.
91	#
92	# Members: design → design-gate. design-gate is a T0 tool (ADR-037 §3): a pure-grep
93	# PRE-build structural gate over design.md + the red-first stubs design writes. It
94	# is BOTH a cycle member AND convergence:gate, so the typed-aggregator preflight
95	# rule (A) is satisfied by binding exit_when directly to it — a single gate, no
96	# separate aggregator needed (contrast build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator, which
97	# rolls up MANY gates). exit_when fires on design-gate.verdict == pass.
98	# max_iterations: 2, on_max: halt (#2176): a contract the gate still rejects is
99	# not built. Nested in delivery_loop (#2271), running out of rounds ends that
100	# loop's round — build is skipped — and the outer loop goes round.
101	#
102	# Feedback: design.design → design.prior_design (self-edge) — mirrors
103	# design_impact_cycle so iter N+1 refines rather than re-creates (#773 lesson).
104	#
105	design_verify_cycle:
106	  type: cycle
107	  description: Verify the design contract is build-ready until design-gate passes
108	  flow:
109	    - design
110	    # #1683: does the design cover what the ISSUE asked for? Design is the only
111	    # reader of the issue, so nothing else confirms the SPECs are a faithful
112	    # statement of the ask. Inside the cycle, so a finding reaches design itself
113	    # on the next iteration.
114	    - spec-coverage
115	    - design-gate
116	  # #1284/ADR-047 multi-condition: BOTH must hold. spec-coverage may gate under
117	  # ADR-040 §5 as amended by #2040 — the standard it judges against is the
118	  # ISSUE, which design cannot re-author, so the only way to converge is to
119	  # actually cover it.
120	  #
121	  # #2366: every stage reports pass or fail, so the rule is `eq pass`. An issue
122	  # spec-coverage cannot read is a fail too; intake already refuses an
123	  # unreadable issue in a real run (#1804).
124	  exit_when:
125	    all:
126	      - { stage: design-gate, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
127	      - { stage: spec-coverage, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
128	  max_iterations: 2
129	  on_max: halt
130	
131	# ─── spec-coverage (leaf, gate) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
132	# Model-judged but admissible on the convergence path (ADR-040 §5 / #2040): its
133	# standard is the issue, produced by intake OUTSIDE this cycle, so the judged
134	# party cannot re-author it.
135	spec-coverage:
136	  gate: auto
137	  roles: [spec_coverage]
138	  # A product owner asks "was what was asked for delivered?" — intent-seeking,
139	  # which is wrong for judging an assertion against a SPEC (the bug there
140	  # survives charity) and exactly right here, where the question IS about intent.
141	  persona: product-owner
142	  stage_timeout_s: 600
143	  router:
144	    timeout_s: 600
145	
146	# ─── test-author (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────────────
147	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
148	# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
149	# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
150	test-author:
151	  gate: auto
152	  roles: [test_author]
153	  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
154	  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
155	  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
156	  blocking: true
157	  stage_timeout_s: 900
158	  router:
159	    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
160	    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
161	    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
162	    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
163	    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
164	    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
165	    timeout_s: 900
166	    max_turns: 0
167	    max_iterations: 4
168	
169	# ─── spec-correspondence (leaf, advisory) ────────────────────────────────────
170	# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not gate. Its finding reaches
171	# test-author on the next iteration through the summary channel.
172	spec-correspondence:
173	  gate: auto
174	  roles: [spec_correspondence]
175	  # #1627: personas were consumed only by review lenses and NO template carried
176	  # a persona: key, so a persona manifest resolved to nothing. This is the first
177	  # stage-level binding. QA assures traceability; it does not test — which is
178	  # what separates it from test-strategist, whose instinct shown a mismatched
179	  # assertion is to repair it and answer yes.
180	  persona: quality-assurance
181	  stage_timeout_s: 600
182	  router:
183	    timeout_s: 600
184	
185	# ─── assertion-integrity (leaf, gate) ────────────────────────────────────────
186	# Mechanical, no model.route — so it MAY gate (ADR-040 §5).
187	assertion-integrity:
188	  gate: auto
189	  roles: [assertion_integrity]
190	  stage_timeout_s: 600
191	
192	# ─── issue-acceptance (leaf, gate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
193	# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
194	# path is allowed for the same reason as spec-coverage (ADR-040 §5 as amended by
195	# #2040): its standard is the issue, which the judged stages cannot re-author.
196	issue-acceptance:
197	  gate: auto
198	  roles: [issue_acceptance]
199	  # Same question spec-coverage asks of the design — "was what was asked for
200	  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
201	  persona: product-owner
202	  stage_timeout_s: 600
203	  router:
204	    timeout_s: 600
205	
206	# ─── build_test_cycle (cycle) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
207	# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 §2/§5): the cycle re-runs build/test then the decomposed
208	# mechanical gates (shape-floor, acceptance-gate, secret-scan) and finally the
209	# gate-aggregator, which collapses every must-pass gate into ONE convergence
210	# verdict. exit_when fires on gate-aggregator.verdict == pass — the ADR-019
211	# fail-closed contract re-expressed as a single composable construct (ADR-040 §5).
212	# (#1129 Change C, ADR-012: the lint/coverage/mutation read-out gates were
213	# DROPPED as cycle members — they were redundant. mutation and lint both run in
214	# the test suite (run-tests.sh --tier all / npm test, which the `test` cycle
215	# member runs), so a lint or mutation regression fails the `test` gate directly.
216	# coverage is NOT folded into the suite — it stays enforced by the dedicated CI
217	# `coverage` job (re-running it inside --tier all would trip the #983 re-entrancy
218	# guard; see ADR-012 "Coverage gating"). The lint-gate/coverage-gate/mutation-gate
219	# plugins remain canonical (ADR-013) but dormant for future reuse.)
220	# The individual gates are NON-blocking (no blocking:true):
221	# they emit verdict-in-artifact (ADR-004) and the cycle iterates-to-fix; the loop
222	# converges via exit_when, never via per-gate hard-blocks. max_iterations: 3.
223	# Nested in delivery_loop (#2271): running out of rounds hands back to that loop,
224	# which goes round from design.
225	build_test_cycle:
226	  type: cycle
227	  description: Build, test, and run the mechanical gates until gate-aggregator passes
228	  flow:
229	    # #2022: test-author runs FIRST. It authors the acceptance assertions from
230	    # the design's SPEC sentences before build implements against them, so the
231	    # code and the assertion are two independent readings rather than two
232	    # artifacts of one. It never sees the diff.
233	    - test-author
234	    # #2034: judges whether each assertion tests what its SPEC SAYS — the one
235	    # link execution cannot reach (a passing test proves the implementation
236	    # satisfies the ASSERTION, never that the assertion satisfies the SENTENCE).
237	    # Before build, because its question needs the requirement and the assertion
238	    # and not the implementation — which at this point does not exist yet, so
239	    # its isolation is a fact of placement rather than a rule to enforce.
240	    - spec-correspondence
241	    - build
242	    - test
243	    - shape-floor
244	    - acceptance-gate
245	    - secret-scan
246	    # #2022: mechanical backstop. The spawn denies build Edit() on the declared
247	    # TESTFILES, but #1919 P5 measured that a Write(...) deny rule matches
248	    # nothing — prevention is incomplete by construction. A fail here makes the
249	    # aggregate non-pass, so the cycle iterates rather than converging on a
250	    # rewritten assertion.
251	    - assertion-integrity
252	    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
253	    # only check after spec-coverage that reads the issue at all. A convergence
254	    # gate, so gate-aggregator's roster makes it must-pass; each unmet
255	    # requirement is a numbered finding.
256	    - issue-acceptance
257	    - gate-aggregator
258	  exit_when:
259	    stage: gate-aggregator
260	    field: verdict
261	    op: eq
262	    value: pass
263	  max_iterations: 3
264	  on_max: continue
265	  # The cycle CONVERGES rather than spinning build(no-op)→…→gate-aggregator(fail)
266	  # because the aggregator's consolidated gate-feedback.md reaches build. B2
267	  # (ADR-040): the gate-aggregator is the SINGLE collector of failure detail,
268	  # merging every failing mechanical gate into one document. It used to arrive
269	  # through a feedback: wire plus a bespoke reader; #1979 retired both — the
270	  # aggregator marks that output `summary: true` (#1976) and the engine injects
271	  # it, framed by verdict, with no per-consumer wiring.
272	# ─── intake (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
273	intake:
274	  gate: auto
275	  roles: [intake]
276	  stage_timeout_s: 600
277	  io:
278	    destinations: [file, stdout]
279	    tail_lines: 200
280	
281	# ─── plan (leaf) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
282	plan:
283	  gate: auto
284	  roles: [planner]
285	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
286	  persona: product-owner
287	  stage_timeout_s: 1200
288	  io:
289	    destinations: [file, stdout]
290	    tail_lines: 200
291	  router:
292	    timeout_s: 300
293	    # 45 (raised from the 25 default, #1442): scope exploration needs
294	    # headroom. The planner is
295	    # also told this budget in its prompt and biased to converge before it runs out.
296	    max_turns: 45
297	
298	# ─── design (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ───────────────────────────────
299	design:
300	  gate: auto
301	  roles: [designer]
302	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
303	  persona: architect
304	  stage_timeout_s: 3900
305	  io:
306	    destinations: [file, stdout]
307	    tail_lines: 200
308	  router:
309	    timeout_s: 600
310	    max_turns: 0
311	
312	# ─── design-gate (leaf, design_verify_cycle member) ──────────────────────────
313	# T0 tool gate (ADR-046, #1218): PRE-build mechanical structural gate. Pure grep
314	# over design.md (NO LLM, NO baseline — ADR-037 §3). Runs the 5 structural
315	# checks (scope non-empty; acceptance block well-formed; every SPEC has a status
316	# — [code], [no-code] or [done] with evidence that exists (ADR-069); every [code]
317	# SPEC declares a TESTFILE; WIRING present/none + paths exist) and reports ALL
318	# violations in ONE pass. verdict-in-artifact; the design_verify_cycle exit_when
319	# reads design-gate.verdict == pass. Bound by role design_gate.
320	design-gate:
321	  gate: auto
322	  roles: [design_gate]
323	  stage_timeout_s: 600
324	  io:
325	    destinations: [file, stdout]
326	    tail_lines: 200
327	
328	# ─── build (leaf, cycle member) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
329	build:
330	  gate: auto
331	  roles: [builder]
332	  # ADR-051: the provider runs the stage as this persona (--agent).
333	  persona: developer
334	  stage_timeout_s: 4200
335	  io:
336	    destinations: [file, stdout]
337	    tail_lines: 200
338	  router:
339	    timeout_s: 900
340	    max_turns: 0
341	
342	# ─── test (leaf, cycle member) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
343	test:
344	  gate: auto
345	  roles: [tester]
346	  stage_timeout_s: 5400
347	  io:
348	    destinations: [file, stdout]
349	    tail_lines: 200
350	
351	# ─── shape-floor (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
352	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1134): un-gameable shape-floor check. verdict-in-artifact.
353	shape-floor:
354	  gate: auto
355	  roles: [shape_floor]
356	  stage_timeout_s: 600
357	  io:
358	    destinations: [file, stdout]
359	    tail_lines: 200
360	
361	# ─── acceptance-gate (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
362	# Mechanical (non-LLM) acceptance-contract gate (ADR-036, #922). No-op pass when
363	# the design acceptance block is absent (its design input is required:false in the
364	# manifest — design already emits the SPEC/WIRING block). Its gate_result feeds
365	# the acceptance→build feedback edge above.
366	# ADR-036 #1188: negctl_timeout_s bounds each SPEC negative-control / reachability
367	# test run (seconds). A timeout is classified INFRA (non-terminal), never a
368	# violation. Override per-run with ZBUILD_NEGCTL_TIMEOUT (env wins).
369	acceptance-gate:
370	  gate: auto
371	  roles: [acceptance_gate]
372	  negctl_timeout_s: 60
373	  stage_timeout_s: 600
374	  io:
375	    destinations: [file, stdout]
376	    tail_lines: 200
377	  router:
378	    timeout_s: 600
379	    max_turns: 10
380	
381	# ─── secret-scan (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────────
382	# T0 tool gate (ADR-040, #1136): blocks hardcoded secrets/.env in the diff.
383	# verdict-in-artifact (skip on empty diff).
384	secret-scan:
385	  gate: auto
386	  roles: [secret_scan]
387	  stage_timeout_s: 600
388	  io:
389	    destinations: [file, stdout]
390	    tail_lines: 200
391	
392	# ─── gate-aggregator (leaf, cycle member) ────────────────────────────────────
393	# T0 convergence aggregator (ADR-040 §2/§5, #1137): collapses the must-pass gate
394	# set into ONE verdict. This is the cycle's exit_when source and the single
395	# merge-blocking construct in the decomposed pipeline. verdict-in-artifact.
396	gate-aggregator:
397	  gate: auto
398	  roles: [gate_aggregator]
399	  stage_timeout_s: 600
400	  io:
401	    destinations: [file, stdout]
402	    tail_lines: 200
403	
404	# ─── review_lenses (map group, ADVISORY) ─────────────────────────────────────
405	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): converted from `type: parallel` to `type: map`.
406	# Each element (security, performance, red-team, correctness, scope) becomes one
407	# work unit dispatched to the review-lens plugin (provides.role: review_lens).
408	# `as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID` maps each element into the env var the review-lens
409	# plugin already reads to derive the lens identity — so the plugin is unchanged
410	# from its per-stage form. This eliminates the five separate lens-* stage
411	# definitions while preserving the same five isolated LLM calls and the same
412	# lens-<element>.json artifact names (ADR-038 §2 isolated-call discipline).
413	#
414	# aggregate: advisory — this group is NEVER on a merge-blocking path (ADR-040 §4).
415	# Convergence is owned by the build_test_cycle's gate-aggregator exit_when above;
416	# the B5 (#1137) no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
417	review_lenses:
418	  type: map
419	  over: lenses
420	  # ADR-051 §2: each lens names the persona it runs as; none is inferred
421	  # from the lens's name.
422	  elements:
423	    - id: security
424	      persona: security
425	    - id: performance
426	      persona: performance
427	    - id: red-team
428	      persona: red-team
429	    - id: correctness
430	      persona: correctness
431	    - id: scope
432	      persona: scope
433	    - id: sre
434	      persona: sre
435	  roles: [review_lens]
436	  as: ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID
437	  max_parallel: 4
438	  on_member_error: continue
439	  aggregate: advisory
440	  stage_timeout_s: 600
441	  io:
442	    destinations: [file]
443	    tail_lines: 200
444	  router:
445	    timeout_s: 300
446	    max_turns: 25
447	
448	# ─── review-aggregator (leaf, ADVISORY) ──────────────────────────────────────
449	# C2 (#1141, ADR-040 §3/§4): merges the review_lenses members' results — the
450	# lens_result set the engine hands it (ADR-055 §1.4, #1842) — into ONE advisory
451	# merge-readiness report (review-report.json + review-report.md). Does NO LLM call
452	# — it merges lens JSON only. Bound by role review_aggregator to
453	# plugins/agent/review-aggregator. Requires lens_result: with no lens result the
454	# engine refuses it, and an empty set reports needs_attention, never "ready"
455	# (#1753). Never recommends a merge action, never blocks.
456	# The report.json filename is unchanged, so merge / pr-delivery consume it as before.
457	review-aggregator:
458	  gate: auto
459	  roles: [review_aggregator]
460	  stage_timeout_s: 600
461	  io:
462	    destinations: [file, stdout]
463	    tail_lines: 200
464	
465	# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
466	# T0 tool stage (ADR-013): opens the pull request; no LLM call.
467	pr:
468	  gate: auto
469	  roles: [pr]
470	  stage_timeout_s: 600
471	  io:
472	    destinations: [file, stdout]
473	    tail_lines: 200
474	
475	# ─── release (always-run, ADR-054 §7) ────────────────────────────────────────
476	# Frees live resources — process groups, locks, handles — and DELETES NOTHING,
477	# so a failed run keeps every byte of its evidence on disk. The teardown plugin
478	# pins its own scope to `release`; `purge` is operator-only and unreachable from
479	# any run path (`zbuild clean --purge`).
480	#
481	# timeout_s is 30 and is load-bearing, not a formality: this stage runs inside
482	# the EXIT trap, so a cleanup hook that blocks would turn Ctrl-C into a hang —
483	# the exact class of bug the mechanism exists to prevent.
484	release:
485	  gate: auto
486	  roles: [teardown]
487	  stage_timeout_s: 30
488	  io:
489	    destinations: [file]
490	    tail_lines: 50
491	
492	# ─── persist (always-run, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ───────────────────────────
493	# Snapshots the artifact area to zbuild/state/issue-<N> and PUSHES it, on every
494	# exit path. Runs AFTER release, and that order is load-bearing: release frees
495	# live resources and must stay fast, while this does network I/O and can block
496	# on auth or a dead remote. Persist last means a bad network can never delay an
497	# abort.
498	#
499	# timeout_s is 120, four times release's 30. A push crosses the network; a
500	# process-group kill does not.
501	persist:
502	  gate: auto
503	  roles: [persist]
504	  stage_timeout_s: 120
505	  io:
506	    destinations: [file]
507	    tail_lines: 50
508	
509	# ─── hydrate (first in flow, ADR-050 §7 / ADR-059 §3) ────────────────────────
510	# Pulls prior artifacts for this issue out of zbuild/state/issue-<N> so each
511	# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and
512	# is NOT always-run — there is nothing to hydrate at the end of a run.
513	#
514	# It fetches origin's copy first, which is what makes a fresh CI clone able to
515	# restore at all; a LOCAL snapshot still wins on read, because it may carry work
516	# an earlier push never delivered.
517	hydrate:
518	  gate: auto
519	  roles: [hydrate]
520	  # #2366: restoring less than all earlier work is reported as fail; the run
521	  # carries on without it rather than stopping.
522	  blocking: false
523	  stage_timeout_s: 600
524	  router:
525	    timeout_s: 60
526	  io:
527	    destinations: [file]
528	    tail_lines: 50
529

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
3	#
4	# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
5	# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
6	# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
7	#
8	#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
9	#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
10	#
11	# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
12	# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
13	# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
14	#
15	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
16	
17	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1
19	
20	# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
21	# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
22	# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
23	# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
24	if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
25	   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
26	   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
28	else
29	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
30	fi
31	
32	_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
33	_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
34	
35	# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
36	# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
37	# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
38	# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
39	# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
40	# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
41	# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)
42	
43	# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
45	_orch_not_implemented() {
46	    local fn_name="$1"
47	    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
48	    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
49	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
51	    fi
52	    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
53	    return 1
54	}
55	
56	# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
57	# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.
58	
59	if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
61	fi
62	
63	if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
65	fi
66	
67	if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
68	    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
69	    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
70	    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
71	    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
72	    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
73	fi
74	
75	if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
77	fi
78	
79	if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
80	    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
81	fi
82	
83	# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84	# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
85	# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
86	# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
87	orch_has_capability() {
88	    local cap="$1"
89	    local caps
90	    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
91	    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
92	        return 0
93	    fi
94	    return 1
95	}
96	
97	# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
98	# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
99	# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
100	#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
101	#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
102	# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
103	_orch_find_backend_dir() {
104	    local alias="$1"
105	    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"
106	
107	    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1
108	
109	    local manifest plugin_dir
110	    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
111	        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
112	        # Check provides.role
113	        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
114	            continue
115	        fi
116	        # Check id or provides.alias match
117	        local id declared_alias
118	        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
119	        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
120	        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
121	            echo "$plugin_dir"
122	            return 0
123	        fi
124	    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)
125	
126	    return 1
127	}
128	
129	# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130	# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
131	# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
132	# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
133	# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
134	# Missing or unreadable backend is misconfigured (no fallback).
135	# If no plugin is found, emits orch.backend.misconfigured and returns 1.
136	orch_load_backend() {
137	    local backend="${1:-}"
138	    local plugin_dir
139	
140	    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
141	        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	
145	    # "sequential" and the long-form alias are retired — emit misconfigured immediately.
146	    # (Build the retired long-form by concatenation so no stale literal appears here.)
147	    local _retired_long="orch-"
148	    _retired_long+="sequential"
149	    if [[ "$backend" == "sequential" || "$backend" == "$_retired_long" ]]; then
150	        if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
151	            emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
152	                "reason=sequential backends retired; use bash-parallel" || true
153	        fi
154	        warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' is misconfigured — sequential backends are retired; configure bash-parallel instead" || true
155	        return 1
156	    fi
157	
158	    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
159	    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
161	        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
162	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
163	            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
164	            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
165	            return 0
166	        fi
167	    fi
168	
169	    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
170	    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
171	    # When ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is set to a directory other than the engine's own
172	    # plugins (e.g. a test temp dir), also search the engine's plugins so that
173	    # backends like bash-parallel remain resolvable without installing them there.
174	    if [[ -z "$plugin_dir" || ! -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
175	        local _engine_plugins="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins"
176	        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-}" != "" && \
177	              "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT}" != "${_engine_plugins}" ]]; then
178	            plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" "${_engine_plugins}" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
179	        fi
180	    fi
181	    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
182	        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
183	        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
184	        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
185	        return 0
186	    fi
187	
188	    # Backend not found — misconfigured, not a silent fallback.
189	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
190	        emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
191	            "reason=no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias $backend" || true
192	    fi
193	    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' misconfigured — not found (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias ${backend})" || true
194	    return 1
195	}
196	
197	# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
198	# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
199	# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
200	# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
201	_orch_load_backend() {
202	    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
203	    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
204	    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
205	    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
206	    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0
207	
208	    local backend
209	
210	    # Get configured backend, falling back to "bash-parallel" if config unavailable
211	    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
212	        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="bash-parallel"
213	    else
214	        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-bash-parallel}"
215	    fi
216	
217	    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
218	    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
219	    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
220	}
221	
222	# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
223	_orch_load_backend
224

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/local_engine.sh — shared dispatch/collect/poll/shutdown for the
3	# local-execution orchestrator backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive).
4	# Extracted from those two plugins in #281 because they had ~80% duplication
5	# and the #269 normaliser fix had to be applied twice (and still missed
6	# orch-mock — caught belatedly in #278). Single source of truth now.
7	#
8	# Pool layout (caller chooses prefix + pid subdir name):
9	#   <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/<slot>.pid       — wrapper subshell PID
10	#   <pool_dir>/results/<slot>.{stdout,stderr,exit,inner_pid}
11	#
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; no set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED=1
16	
17	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
19	
20	# Defensive source: warn (scripts/lib/helpers.sh).
21	if ! declare -F warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
22	    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
23	fi
24	
25	# Load process-group kill helpers (zbuild_pg_kill, zbuild_pid_kill).
26	if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
28	fi
29	
30	# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
31	_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
32	    date +%s%N
33	    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"
34	    openssl rand -hex 8 2>/dev/null || printf '%05d%05d%05d' $RANDOM $RANDOM $RANDOM
35	}
36	
37	
38	# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>
39	# Dispatches <work_unit> (must be an executable file path) in a background
40	# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate
41	# SIGTERM/EXIT to the inner process.
42	#
43	# Output: prints slot_id to stdout AND sets the global _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID.
44	# Callers needing the slot_id after dispatch (e.g. for downstream telemetry)
45	# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`
46	# forks a subshell whose EXIT trap (installed by test-helpers.sh or similar)
47	# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
48	# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)
49	#
50	# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
51	_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
52	    local pool_dir="$1"
53	    local pid_subdir="$2"
54	    local work_unit="$3"
55	    local caller_tag="${4:-orch_local}"
56	
57	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""
58	
59	    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
60	        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
61	        return 1
62	    fi
63	
64	    # Ensure pool dirs exist even if the caller skipped pre-spawn.
65	    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
66	        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
67	        return 1
68	    }
69	
70	    local slot_id
71	    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
72	    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
73	
74	    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to
75	    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.
76	    (
77	        local rc=0 inner=0
78	        # #2108: dispatched from a `<<< "$roles_out"` loop — never its stdin.
79	        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &
80	        inner=$!
81	        echo "$inner" > "${result_base}.inner_pid"
82	        trap 'kill -KILL "$inner" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT INT TERM
83	        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
84	        trap - EXIT INT TERM
85	        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
86	    ) &
87	    local worker_pid=$!
88	    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
89	    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
90	    echo "$slot_id"
91	    return 0
92	}
93	
94	# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
95	# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
96	# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
97	#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
98	#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
99	#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
100	#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
101	# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
102	# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
103	_orch_local_collect_results() {
104	    local pool_dir="$1"
105	    local pid_subdir="$2"
106	    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
107	    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
108	
109	    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }
110	
111	    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
112	    local deadline=0
113	    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))
114	
115	    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
116	    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
117	        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
118	        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
119	        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
120	        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
121	        inner_pid=""
122	        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"
123	
124	        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
125	            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
126	                if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
127	                    zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
128	                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
129	                else
130	                    kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
131	                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
132	                fi
133	                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
134	                break
135	            fi
136	            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
137	        done
138	
139	        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
140	        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
141	        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
142	        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
143	            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
144	        else
145	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
146	        fi
147	    done
148	
149	    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
150	        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
151	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
152	        return 0
153	    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
154	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
155	        return 1
156	    else
157	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	}
161	
162	# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
163	# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
164	# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
165	_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
166	    local pool_dir="$1"
167	    local pid_subdir="$2"
168	
169	    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0
170	
171	    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
172	    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
173	        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
174	        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
175	        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
176	        inner_pid=""
177	        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
178	            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
179	        if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
180	            zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
181	            [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
182	        else
183	            kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
184	            [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
185	        fi
186	    done
187	    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
188	    return 0
189	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
3	# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
4	# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
16	#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
22	# Collects all results with orch_collect.
23	# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
24	#
25	# Returns:
26	#   0 — all succeeded
27	#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
28	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_fanout() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
32	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
33	    # | infra_failed | failed.
34	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
35	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
36	    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
37	    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()
38	
39	    local role platform plugin_dir wu
40	    while IFS= read -r role; do
41	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
42	        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
43	            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
44	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
45	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
46	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
47	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
48	            any_plugin_found=true
49	
50	            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
51	                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
52	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
53	                continue
54	            }
55	            work_units+=("$wu")
56	
57	            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
58	                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
59	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
60	                continue
61	            }
62	            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
63	            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
64	        done
65	    done <<< "$roles_out"
66	
67	    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
68	        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
69	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
71	        return 1
72	    fi
73	
74	    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
75	    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
76	    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
77	        local collect_rc=0
78	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
79	        orch_collect "$pool_id" || collect_rc=$?
80	
81	        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial named on
82	        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
83	        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
84	            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
85	            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
86	            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
87	            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
88	        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
89	            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
90	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
91	        else
92	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
93	        fi
94	    fi
95	
96	    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
97	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
98

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
3	# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
4	# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
16	#   stage      — stage name
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit at a time via orch_dispatch + orch_collect.
22	# Halts on first failure (does not continue to next platform/role).
23	# Always calls orch_shutdown on exit (success or failure).
24	# Artifact enforcement happens per work unit inside plugin_hook_call (#1906).
25	#
26	# Returns:
27	#   0 — all succeeded
28	#   1 — any collect/dispatch failure
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_sequential() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
32	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
33	    # | infra_failed | failed.
34	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
35	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
36	    local any_plugin_found=false
37	
38	    local role platform plugin_dir wu prc
39	    while IFS= read -r role; do
40	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
41	        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
42	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
43	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
44	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
45	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
46	            any_plugin_found=true
47	
48	            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
49	                warn "sequential: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
50	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
51	                return 1
52	            }
53	
54	            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
55	                warn "sequential: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
56	                rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
57	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
58	                return 1
59	            }
60	
61	            prc=0
62	            orch_collect "$pool_id" || prc=$?
63	            rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
64	
65	            if [[ $prc -ne 0 ]]; then
66	                warn "sequential: stage=$stage role=$role platform=$platform failed (rc=$prc)" || true
67	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
68	                return 1
69	            fi
70	
71	        done
72	    done <<< "$roles_out"
73	
74	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
75	    $any_plugin_found || { _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"; return 1; }
76	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
77	    return 0
78	}

2	# core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh — data-driven map over any declared list dimension (issue #1285)
3	# ADR-047: generalizes fanout (platforms) to arbitrary declared dimensions.
4	# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_dimension ─────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Resolves the iteration list for the given dimension name.
15	# For "platforms": uses _DETECTED_PLATFORMS (set by runner before dispatch).
16	# For other names: uses _MAP_DIM_<name> array if set; otherwise empty.
17	# Prints one element per line; no output = empty dimension.
18	_strategy_map_resolve_dimension() {
19	    local dim="${1:-platforms}"
20	    if [[ "$dim" == "platforms" ]]; then
21	        local p
22	        for p in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]+"${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"}"; do
23	            [[ -n "$p" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
24	        done
25	        return 0
26	    fi
27	    # Arbitrary dimension: caller must export _MAP_DIM_<name> as an array.
28	    # Validate dimension name to prevent variable-name injection.
29	    if [[ ! "$dim" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
30	        warn "map: invalid dimension name: ${dim}" || true
31	        return 1
32	    fi
33	    # Read the caller's _MAP_DIM_<name> array by reference (Bash 5+ floor — see
34	    # scripts/lib/compat.sh). The name was validated above, guarding the target.
35	    # The array lives in the caller's scope (same sourced shell). Guarded
36	    # expansion tolerates an unset target under the caller's `set -u`.
37	    local -n _ref="_MAP_DIM_${dim}"
38	    local elem
39	    for elem in "${_ref[@]+"${_ref[@]}"}"; do
40	        [[ -n "$elem" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$elem"
41	    done
42	}
43	
44	# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_max ───────────────────────────────────────────────
45	# Resolves the max_parallel concurrency cap for a map group.
46	# Input: raw max value from template (_TPL_MAP_MAX_<gid>), e.g. "4", "auto", "".
47	# Mirrors _parallel_resolve_max (parallel-orchestrator.sh) EXACTLY so map and
48	# parallel groups agree on the cap and its fail-safe:
49	#   - explicit positive integer  → used as-is (then capped at _PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP)
50	#   - "auto" / empty             → ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS env override, else CPU count
51	#   - ANYTHING else (non-numeric typo, "0", negative) → CLAMPED TO 1 (fail-safe).
52	# #1312 (Copilot): an invalid template value must NOT silently remove the cap by
53	# falling through to CPU-count concurrency — that is the opposite of safe. Clamp to 1.
54	_strategy_map_resolve_max() {
55	    local raw="${1:-}"
56	    # #1312 (Copilot): reuse the parallel path's readonly cap so map and parallel
57	    # stay in sync if it ever changes — don't duplicate the literal. Falls back to 8
58	    # only when map.sh is sourced standalone (unit tests) without the parallel module.
59	    local cap="${_PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP:-8}"
60	    local max="$raw"
61	    # "auto" is an explicit request for the CPU-based default (map-specific alias);
62	    # normalise it to empty so the empty-branch resolves the default.
63	    [[ "$max" == "auto" ]] && max=""
64	    if [[ -z "$max" ]]; then
65	        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
66	            max="$ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS"
67	        else
68	            max="$( { nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null; } | head -1 )"  # sigpipe-ok: writer emits exactly one line
69	            [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=4
70	        fi
71	    fi
72	    # Fail-safe clamp: any non-positive-integer (typo, "0", negative) → 1.
73	    [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=1
74	    (( max > cap )) && max=$cap
75	    printf '%s' "$max"
76	}
