78	# ─── _strategy_run_map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
79	# Usage: _strategy_run_map <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root> \
80	#                          [dimension] [env_target] [max_parallel] [on_member_error]
81	#   pool_id          — caller-supplied, already validated. Used as the base for
82	#                      per-batch sub-pool ids ("<base>-b<N>", truncated to fit the
83	#                      64-char backend limit). The FIFO-batch loop below spawns and
84	#                      shuts down one sub-pool per batch via orch_spawn/orch_shutdown;
85	#                      the caller's own pool_id is also orch_shutdown at the end.
86	#   stage            — stage name (e.g. "intake")
87	#   roles_out        — newline-delimited list of role names
88	#   state_file       — path to pipeline state file
89	#   plugins_root     — path to plugins directory
90	#   dimension        — list name to iterate (default: "platforms")
91	#   env_target       — optional env var name to set to each element per work unit
92	#                      (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2: generic dimension→env mapping declared
93	#                      by the template's `as:` field; empty = no extra env). The
94	#                      strategy is element-name-agnostic — it never hardcodes a var name.
95	#   max_parallel     — concurrency cap (issue #1312): "auto"/empty = CPU-based cap;
96	#                      integer = explicit cap. Enforced via a FIFO-pool batch loop
97	#                      (mirrors ADR-039 parallel_group_run FIFO pool semantics).
98	#   on_member_error  — "collect" (default) or "continue" (issue #1312).
99	#                      continue: a failing element does NOT abort the group (return 0);
100	#                      collect:  any failure is propagated (return 1/2).
101	#                      Unknown values are NOT validated — they fall through to collect
102	#                      (the conservative default), matching parallel_group_run which
103	#                      also silently defaults unknown values to its safe branch.
104	#                      Mirrors parallel_group_run on_member_error semantics (ADR-039).
105	#
106	# Dispatches one work unit per role×element pair.
107	# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
108	#
109	# Returns:
110	#   0 — all succeeded, OR on_member_error=continue (even with failures)
111	#   1 — all failed (only when on_member_error=collect)
112	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail; only when on_member_error=collect)
113	#   3 — empty dimension (no elements to iterate; caller/runner maps to no-op 0)
114	#   4 — no plugin found for any role
115	#   5 — invalid/unknown dimension name (fail-closed; runner surfaces as failure)
116	#   6 — infrastructure failure (orch_spawn failed for a batch sub-pool). Fail-closed:
117	#       NOT subject to on_member_error — an infra failure is never a member outcome.
118	#   Two members that would run under one unit name (#1706) are refused before
119	#   any member starts: rc 1 (ADR-054 §4 — rc says only "failed"); the
120	#   strategy.unit_name_conflict event says why. Not subject to on_member_error.
121	# _map_unit_element <var> <role_count> <role> <element> — sets <var> to the part
122	# of a member's unit name after the stage (#1706): the element, or
123	# <role>.<element> when the map runs more than one role. No subshell per member.
124	_map_unit_element() {
125	    if [[ "$2" -gt 1 ]]; then printf -v "$1" '%s.%s' "$3" "$4"; else printf -v "$1" '%s' "$4"; fi
126	}
127	
128	_strategy_run_map() {
129	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
130	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
131	    # | infra_failed | failed.
132	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
133	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
134	    local dimension="${6:-platforms}" env_target="${7:-}"
135	    local max_raw="${8:-}" on_member_error="${9:-collect}"
136	    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false
137	
138	    # Resolve the iteration list. Capture output AND rc explicitly — a process
139	    # substitution would discard the resolver's status, collapsing an invalid
140	    # dimension (rc=2) into the empty path (rc=3) and masking a fail-closed error.
141	    local _resolved _res_rc
142	    _resolved="$(_strategy_map_resolve_dimension "$dimension")"; _res_rc=$?
143	    if [[ $_res_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
144	        # Invalid/unknown dimension name — fail closed. Distinct from empty (rc=3);
145	        # the runner does NOT map rc=5 to 0, so this surfaces as a real failure.
146	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
147	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="bad_dimension"
148	        return 1
149	    fi

I've thoroughly searched the repository for all items related to issue #1801 (stage timeout and orchestrator changes). Here are my findings:

### 1. **core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh** (Lines 510-540 - Watchdog/Kill Section)

**Location:** `/home/runner/.zbuild/repos/ezigus/zBuild/issues/1801/worktree/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh:513-532`

```bash
        ) &
        _lc_hook_pid=$!
        ( set +m; sleep "$_lc_hook_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
        _lc_wd_pid=$!
        set +m
        # Restore runner's monitor mode: set +m above always clears it, even when
        # ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1 had it enabled before this call.
        (( _lc_m_before == 1 )) && set -m
        wait "$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
        # #2333: the group leader exiting does not mean its group members did.
        # A child that ignored TERM would survive if the watchdog is cancelled before
        # it delivers KILL, so KILL the whole group now.
        kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_wd_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$_lc_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
            emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "timeout_s=${_lc_hook_to}" \
                "disposition=timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
```

The watchdog mechanism (lines 515-527) uses:
- `zbuild_pg_kill` with a grace period (10 seconds for the hook, 1 second for the watchdog)
- Process group targets via `-PGID` notation
- `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"` as a backstop

- `§9(stage_timeout_s)` - plugin_hook_call has per-dispatch watchdog for run hook, uses zbuild_pg_kill
- `§9(precedence)` - template stage_timeout_s > ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S > 5400 s default

- `§(router.timeout_s)` - load_template sets _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* from router.timeout_s

### 8. **scripts/lib/proc-group.sh**

**Location:** `/home/runner/.zbuild/repos/ezigus/zBuild/issues/1801/worktree/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh`

**Key functions:**

- `zbuild_pg_resolve <pid>` (lines 28-50) - Resolves a process's PGID

- `zbuild_pid_kill <pid> [grace_s]` (lines 159-163) - TERM then KILL a single PID

**Grace period mechanism:**
- Default grace: 1 second
- Polling: 10 iterations × 0.1s = 1 second max wait before KILL
- Used throughout: 10s for hooks, 1s for watchdogs

**Location:** `/home/runner/.zbuild/repos/ezigus/zBuild/issues/1801/worktree/config/event-schema.json`

Pool timeout collection uses `zbuild_pg_kill`:

if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then

Exit code 124 is set when timeout occurs (line 133).

The repository implements issue #1801 (stage timeout enforcement) through:

#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
_orch_local_collect_results() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
    local deadline=0
    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))

    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"

        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
                if declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                    zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true
                else
                    kill -TERM "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill -TERM "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
                fi
                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
                break
            fi
            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
        done

        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi

local slot_id
    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"

    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to

# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
_runner_status_comment_reap() {
    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        local i
        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
            sleep 0.1
        done
        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}
